component.name: Ignis
component.summary: Install and set up apps for Bazzite

description.p: Ignis is a one-stop installer for Bazzite. It detects your graphics hardware and offers a curated list of gaming, emulation, media and streaming applications that can each be installed with a single click, without ever opening a terminal.

Ignis installs software on your behalf. To do that it runs standard package commands on the host system — such as installing Flatpaks from Flathub or running Bazzite's own setup recipes — and it always shows you the exact command it is about to run, streams the live output, and keeps a full log you can read afterwards.

ul.li: Flathub
Bazzite's built-in setup recipes
GitHub releases, with automatic update checks
Vetted configuration scripts bundled with Ignis

description.p: Connecting to a NAS now works on Bazzite.

ul.li: Setting up a NAS at /mnt/nas failed because that folder is a shortcut to somewhere else on Bazzite, which the automatic connection would not accept. Ignis now uses the real location, and /mnt/nas keeps working as before.

description.p: Readable errors, and a NAS connection that explains itself.

ul.li: Error windows can always be closed and scrolled again. A long command could previously push the buttons off the bottom of the window.
Connecting to a NAS now tells you what actually went wrong — that the folder path is wrong, or this computer is not allowed — instead of a message telling you to read the system journal.
Connecting to a NAS no longer insists on NFS version 4.1, which fails on a NAS left at its default setting.
A failed NAS connection no longer leaves a half-finished setup behind that looked like it had worked.

description.p: Jellyfin Server, and an important security fix.

ul.li: Jellyfin Server: turn this computer into your own private streaming service, watched from any screen in the house.
Security: connecting to a NAS no longer passes what you typed to a privileged command in a way that could be abused. Please update.
Connecting to a NAS now refuses to mount over important folders or non-empty ones, and can no longer hang if the NAS stops answering mid-setup.
Services only ask for your password to enable start-at-boot once, not on every reinstall.

description.p: Connecting to a network drive, and your own comics library.

ul.li: Connect to a NAS over NFS: the folder appears locally, comes back after a restart, and never holds up startup when the NAS is off.
Komga, a server for your comics, manga and e-books, read through a web browser.
Apps can now ask a couple of questions before installing, for things only you know — like where your files are.

description.p: Adds Tailscale, which lets your other devices reach this computer securely from anywhere without opening ports on your router.
Adds an optional set of high-quality AV1 conversion settings for HandBrake, which keep your original audio and add a compatible surround track alongside it.
A bigger catalogue, explained in plain language.

ul.li: Nine more apps, including Moonlight to pair with Sunshine, Vesktop for Discord screen sharing with sound, VLC, Lutris, Prism Launcher and OpenRGB.
Every app now explains what it is, why you might want it, and when you can skip it — written for people arriving from Windows.
Chat apps have their own section instead of sitting under System.
Installed apps now have an Open button, so you can start them straight from Ignis.
Any installed app can be given a desktop shortcut with a single switch.

description.p: Keeping things up to date, and showing what your machine is.

ul.li: Ignis now checks for its own new versions and can update itself, instead of needing a manual download.
Apps installed from Flathub are now checked for updates too, not just those from GitHub.
The main screen now shows your actual graphics card, processor, memory and system version.
Flathub installs failed because the flathub remote exists in both the user and system installations; Ignis now says which one to use.
Bazzite recipes (EmuDeck, Sunshine) opened a menu that needed a terminal; Ignis now runs them with an explicit action.
A recipe that printed a menu error but exited successfully is no longer reported as an install that worked.

description.p: CI maintenance: updated GitHub Actions dependencies to versions that run on Node.js 24, ahead of Node.js 20's removal from GitHub Actions runners. No user-facing changes.

ul.li: Browse a curated catalog of gaming, emulation, media, streaming and system apps.
Install from Flathub, Bazzite's own setup recipes, GitHub releases, or bundled setup scripts.
See the exact command before it runs, watch its output live, and keep a full log.
Check for and apply updates to apps installed from GitHub.
Graphics card detection, so apps meant for other hardware are marked.
